title: Occlusion removal and image enhancement for tunnel linings
subtitle: Intelligent infrastructure inspection
shortTitle: Occlusion removal and image enhancement for tunnel linings
summary: Occlusions from pipelines, equipment, and other objects in tunnel-lining scans obscure surface textures and hinder the identification of visible defects such as water leakage. This study constructs paired data using real scans and occluding objects, removes occlusions and reconstructs lining textures through conditional reverse diffusion and local soft blending, and examines the effects of enhanced images on downstream defect detection. The results demonstrate texture and joint restoration under different occlusion conditions, as well as changes in water-leakage detection confidence following image enhancement.

blocks.text: Occlusions from pipelines, equipment, and other objects in tunnel-lining scans obscure surface textures and hinder the identification of visible defects such as water leakage. This study constructs paired data using real scans and occluding objects, removes occlusions and reconstructs lining textures through conditional reverse diffusion and local soft blending, and examines the effects of enhanced images on downstream defect detection. The results demonstrate texture and joint restoration under different occlusion conditions, as well as changes in water-leakage detection confidence following image enhancement.

media.alt: Paired data constructed from real scans and occluding objects
media.label: Figure 1 Paired data constructed from real scans and occluding objects
media.caption: Real occluding objects are combined with visible lining backgrounds to form paired samples, retaining a known background reference for the designated covered regions.

media.alt: Conditional reverse diffusion and local soft blending
media.label: Figure 2 Conditional reverse diffusion and local soft blending
media.caption: The encoder and decoder predict noise, and conditional reverse diffusion progressively generates the image. A soft mask blends the original and generated images to complete designated regions while preserving the unoccluded background.

media.alt: Results of structural occlusion removal and image enhancement
media.label: Figure 3 Results of structural occlusion removal and image enhancement
media.caption: The complete panels a–h show paired inputs and outputs for occlusions caused by pipelines, cables, personnel, and electrical equipment. The results show continuity in joints, textures, and grayscale values after occlusion removal.

blocks.text: The illustrated water-leakage target receives a higher prediction confidence after occlusion removal, indicating that image enhancement improves the visibility of defect features at this location and can provide clearer input for downstream detection.

media.alt: Water-leakage detection before and after image inpainting
media.label: Figure 4 Water-leakage detection before and after image inpainting
media.caption: The left image uses the occluded input, and the right image uses the inpainted input. Green boxes and numbers indicate detection regions and prediction confidence, respectively. After inpainting, the prediction confidence for the illustrated water-leakage target increases from 0.62 to 0.87, and the detection box adjusts to the visible texture.
